verdict.rationale: cubic documents on-demand triggering: you comment `@cubic-dev-ai review this PR` or tag the bot in PR comments to trigger reviews. It also lets you choose which repositories it reviews, and cubic.yaml controls review behavior and ignore patterns. Reviews otherwise run automatically on every new PR, and nothing in the evidence shows skipping drafts or filtering by branch or label. Missing for 10: documented draft-PR skipping, branch-based review filters, label-based review filters, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the trigger controls.

support.subject: As a developer, I control when reviews run — skip drafts, trigger on demand, filter by branch or label — so the bot shows up only when wanted

citations.quote: Post this comment on GitHub to start a review:
Interact with cubic in PR comments to ask questions, trigger reviews, and fix issues.
cubic.yaml lives in the root of your repository and becomes the source of truth for AI review behavior, ignore patterns, PR descriptions, and custom agents.
Select the repositories you want cubic to review.
